prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1391; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Driver 1 was operating a sedan southbound when it struck the front of a pickup truck traveling northbound in the same lane, a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. Driver 2, the operator of the pickup, was present at the scene and confirmed the sequence of events as Driver 1 described them. Two independent witnesses gave statements consistent with that account, and scene photographs were taken and placed in the file. Passenger was seated in the rear of the sedan and was also confirmed present by the responding officers and both witnesses.

Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness shortly after the impact and was transported for evaluation. The complaint is consistent with the kind and force of a frontal impact of this type. Damage to the front of the sedan and the front of the pickup corresponds to the reported point and direction of contact. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported by any party. Records checked at the scene show Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the sedan.
